claims.text: Conway's law is a canonical observation: the structure of a system tends to mirror the communication structure of the organisation that builds it. It describes a tendency, not a rule mapping one service to one team.
claims.source_hint: Conway's law as commonly stated in software architecture literature; glossary conways-law; DECISIONS.md 2026-10-22 (bare reference, no name or year)

claims.text: At stage-3 Đơn Hàng runs three services: DonHang.Api (Ordering and Catalog modules; other code reaches Catalog only through ICatalog), DonHang.Notifications and DonHang.Payments.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 STAGE.md 'A modular monolith with two services split off'

claims.text: docs/team/sprint-example.md lines 3-4: the team is one product owner, one scrum master, four developers and one tester; lines 14-18 assign an API endpoint, an app button and notification work to Dev 1-4 on one board, named by number, not by service.
ADR 0003 line 5 and ADR 0002 line 5 name the same decider, 'trưởng nhóm' (team lead); neither ADR names a team per service.

ADR 0003 lines 13-17: refunds must meet YC-7, YC-9, YC-10, and the payment gateway's API key and money rows are the most sensitive part of the system. The payment gateway ('cổng thanh toán') is the outside service that moves the money.
ADR 0002 lines 17-21: another service (Payments) must also message customers, and a slow or failing email server takes resources from the process that takes orders.

ADRs 0002 and 0003 split services for their own reasons (a second service must also message customers, email failures kept from order taking, refund requirements, the gateway's key); none is a team. The docs describe one team and one decider, no team per service.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 3; ADR 0002 lines 17-21, ADR 0003 lines 13-17, sprint-example.md lines 3-4 @ stage-3

claims.text: When one team owns several services, a change across them is a conversation inside the team (same daily, same sprint board); the split keeps the network's costs (calls that can fail or be slow, one more thing to build, deploy and watch) but adds no waiting between people.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 4; management.l1.scrum-from-junior-seat; ADR 0002 Hệ quả @ stage-3 (calls can fail; extra image, pipeline, database, dashboard)

claims.text: When several teams share one module, each change needs them to agree first; to avoid the wait each team tends to add code where it can change without asking, and with no single owner the module's boundary tends to blur.

When a team grows into several, drawing module and team boundaries together lets each team change its part without waiting, except when the contract where they meet has to change; so the team's shape is an architectural driver, and a change in it reopens boundaries.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 5; design.l4.architectural-drivers (team size listed as a driver)

claims.text: At stage-3 Catalog is a module inside DonHang.Api reached through ICatalog, so it already has a boundary a second team could be drawn along.
claims.source_hint: STAGE.md @ stage-3 ('Catalog (DonHang.Catalog, reached only through ICatalog)'); design.l4.where-boundaries-are-enforced

claims.text: Trade-offs: one team with three services pays the network's costs for the ADRs' reasons, without waiting; a team per service adds agreements on the message; several teams in one module agree on every change; teams along module boundaries agree only when a contract changes.

Choices: with four developers keep Catalog a module unless its own drivers call for a split; with a second team, draw its boundary along Catalog's module boundary and decide a service split separately; do not add teams per service while one team can plan all the work.
claims.source_hint: Outline items 3-5; DECISIONS.md depth_notes (no team types)

claims.text: Services buy independence in releasing, in running more copies of one part without the others, and in failing, and charge the network's costs; they cannot remove waiting between teams when there is only one team.

sprint-example.md line 17 (stop notifications for cancelled orders) depends on line 14 (the cancel endpoint); the API tells Notifications about an order by a message, so separate teams would have to agree on what that message says.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/sprint-example.md lines 14, 17 @ stage-3; OrderMessage is the contract between API and Notifications (design.l4.distributed-monolith)
